candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a). The previous permit will be expired on October 31, 2021. The existing permit is administratively continued until this permit is issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: FY2025 falls after the stated expiration date; whether limits and monitoring obligations derive from the administratively continued prior permit versus a reissued permit—and when reissuance takes effect—determines which enforceable limits apply (A), which monitoring requirements were in force (B), and what monitoring evidence was expected for no-result cases (C).

candidates.exact_span: NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable enforceable limit for a parameter may depend on which of the three sources (ELGs, WQBELs, or prior permit) is deemed more stringent; different readings of this selection rule change the numeric limit used for exceedance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a WQBEL is numerical or narrative affects whether an enforceable numeric comparison is applicable for reported measurements (A) and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified when no ordinary numeric comparison is possible (C).

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS and BOD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies TSS and BOD as parameters subject to technology-based limits rather than WQBELs; interpretation of which parameters carry enforceable TBELs changes limit applicability (A) and which parameters' monitoring obligations and missing-evidence expectations are in scope (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for E. coli bacteria, pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies E. coli, pH, and TRC as WQBEL parameters; different interpretation of limit type and whether limits are numeric or narrative changes applicable limit selection (A) and monitoring or no-data semantics for those parameters (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require TBELs to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two. In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether ELGs or BPJ governs TBEL derivation for this discharge affects the numeric limit values assigned to TSS and BOD and thus which reported measurements exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: EPA establishes limitations based on the following technology-based controls: BPT, BCT, and BAT.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which technology level (BPT, BCT, or BAT) applies to a given pollutant or discharge class determines the stringency of technology-based limits and therefore the enforceable numeric values used for compliance comparison.
